definition: Literally 'to sleep with each other'; the standard polite German euphemism for having sexual intercourse.
notes: The most neutral and widely used German euphemism for sex; appropriate in almost any register outside clinical writing.

definition: Literally 'to go to bed'; used with a partner referent ('mit jemandem ins Bett gehen') as a circumlocution for having sex.
english_term: to go to bed with someone
notes: Without a partner referent the phrase simply means retiring to sleep; the sexual reading is entirely context-dependent.

definition: Literally 'to be together'; primarily denotes being in a romantic partnership, implying an ongoing sexual relationship rather than a single act.
english_term: to be together / to be an item
notes: Rarely used to describe a single sex act; more commonly refers to the relationship as a whole. Teenagers use this to signal exclusive couplehood.

definition: Calque of 'to make love'; a romantically framed German euphemism for sexual intercourse emphasizing emotional intimacy.
notes: Direct borrowing/calque from the English expression; fully naturalized in German. The romantic connotation is preserved; cruder synonyms are preferred when emotional distance is implied.

definition: Literally 'to become intimate'; a polite euphemism for initiating sexual activity, often implying a first sexual encounter between partners.
english_term: to get intimate / to become intimate
notes: Slightly clinical in tone relative to other euphemisms in this set; common in relationship advice, journalism, and counseling discourse.

definition: Reflexive verb meaning 'to enjoy oneself' or 'to amuse oneself'; deployed as a coy, somewhat old-fashioned euphemism for engaging in sexual activity.
english_term: to have a good time / to enjoy oneself
notes: The sexual reading is always context-dependent; the word is used far more often in purely non-sexual recreational senses. The sexual euphemism feels mildly dated.

definition: Literally 'physical love' or 'bodily love'; a formal-register euphemism for sexual intercourse or physical sexual intimacy.
notes: Typically contrasted with 'geistige Liebe' (spiritual love) in philosophical or relationship-counseling discourse; more formal than conversational.

definition: Literally 'physical closeness' or 'physical proximity'; the mildest German euphemism in this set, implying intimate touch that may or may not include sexual intercourse.
notes: Preferred in therapeutic, medical, and relationship-advice contexts precisely because it does not commit to naming intercourse; also used for non-sexual affectionate touch.

definition: Phrase meaning 'to exchange tenderness' or 'to exchange caresses'; a delicate euphemism for affectionate erotic contact that stops short of explicitly naming intercourse.
notes: 'Zärtlichkeiten' (pl.) encompasses kisses, embraces, and light erotic touch; the phrase is used in both non-sexual affectionate and sexual foreplay contexts.

definition: Literally 'shepherd's little hour'; an archaic-flavored German euphemism for a brief, often stolen amorous or sexual tryst.
notes: Originates in German pastoral poetry tradition where shepherds enjoyed idle amorous interludes; today it is used with ironic or humorous distance and carries a distinctly old-fashioned charm.

definition: Literally 'afternoon nap'; used as a humorous or coy euphemism for an afternoon sexual encounter.
notes: The literal meaning (a brief after-lunch sleep) remains the dominant reading; the sexual euphemism is activated entirely by context or a knowing tone.

definition: Crude idiom meaning 'to push a number'; colloquial slang for having sex, with 'Nummer' as slang for a sex act and 'schieben' (to push/shove) adding a blunt physical connotation.
notes: 'Nummer' as slang for a sex act is the core term; 'schieben' makes it cruder than 'eine Nummer machen'. Widespread in informal German male speech.

definition: Idiom 'to do a number'; crude-neutral slang for having sex, slightly less physically blunt than 'eine Nummer schieben' but equally colloquial.
english_term: to do it / to get it on
notes: Variant of 'eine Nummer schieben'; 'machen' (to make/do) is milder than 'schieben' (to push). Both phrases treat sex as an activity ('Nummer') to be performed.

definition: Direct English loanword for a brief, hasty sexual encounter; fully naturalized in German colloquial speech.
notes: Appears without quotation marks in German print and conversation; one of the more successful English sexual loanwords in German.

definition: Literally 'to lay (someone) flat'; crude German slang for having sex with someone, implying a dominant, conquering perspective.
notes: The subject is framed as the active agent laying the other person down; carries misogynistic connotations when used by men about women. Common in locker-room register.

definition: Literally 'to lay (someone) on their back'; a crude idiom for having sex with someone with connotations of overcoming or seducing them.
notes: Shares a secondary non-sexual meaning of 'to cheat or dupe someone' (to overcome them); in the sexual sense, the conquest framing is explicit and the subject takes the active role.

definition: Literally 'relationship maintenance'; a wryly bureaucratic German euphemism for sex within a committed relationship, framing physical intimacy as a household duty or upkeep activity.
english_term: keeping the spark alive / relationship maintenance sex
notes: Humor derives from treating sex as a chore analogous to changing the air filter; used self-deprecatingly by couples. More common in online discourse than spoken German.

definition: Literally 'love play'; a romantic German euphemism for erotic activity between partners, encompassing foreplay and the broader sexual encounter.
notes: 'Spiel' (play/game) implies mutual, playful engagement rather than unilateral action; can refer specifically to foreplay or to the entire sexual encounter depending on context.

definition: Literally 'night of love'; a romantic and literary German euphemism for a night of sexual intimacy between partners.
english_term: a night of love / a passionate night
notes: Higher literary register than conversational German; appears frequently in romance novels, song lyrics, and poetry. Less likely in informal spoken use.

definition: Literally 'act of love'; a standard German euphemism for the sexual act, especially penetrative intercourse.
english_term: the act of love / the sex act
notes: More formal and quasi-clinical than 'Liebe machen'; preferred in journalistic, educational, and public-health contexts where a non-crude but non-clinical term is needed.

definition: Literally 'to have traffic'; shortened from 'Geschlechtsverkehr haben' (to have sexual intercourse); a formal to semi-clinical German euphemism for sex.
english_term: to have intercourse / to have sexual relations
notes: 'Geschlechtsverkehr' is the full clinical term for sexual intercourse; 'Verkehr' alone in this sense is a recognized ellipsis. High technical score reflects its clinical origin despite being a common euphemism.

definition: Latin phrase for 'caught in the act'; used in German specifically to mean catching someone during sexual intercourse or in a compromising sexual situation.
english_term: in flagrante delicto / caught in the act
notes: Derived from Latin legal terminology ('in flagrante delicto'); in modern German colloquial use the sexual application dominates over the general criminal law sense. The full Latin form is also used.

definition: Literally 'under the duvet/blanket'; a coy German euphemism for sexual activity that implies intimacy by referencing its domestic spatial context.
notes: Evokes domestic bedroom intimacy and is often deployed humorously; the vagueness is the point — naming the location rather than the act preserves plausible deniability.

definition: Literally 'between the sheets'; a German euphemism for sexual activity equivalent to the English phrase, implying intercourse by referencing the bed linen.
notes: Likely a calque of the English 'between the sheets'; slightly less common than 'unter der Bettdecke' in everyday German speech. Both operate on the same bedroom-location displacement strategy.

definition: Idiom meaning 'to go on the street' or 'to go out on the rounds'; used in German slang for a sex worker going out to solicit clients, or more loosely for going out to seek casual sexual encounters.
english_term: to walk the streets / to go on the game
notes: Ambiguous between sex-work soliciting and general sexual cruising; the former reading is dominant in traditional slang usage. Relatively low current recognition reflects generational fading of the term.
